context: This example continues linear probing with a step size of 1. Lookup starts at key % 100 and stops at a genuinely empty bucket, None. Here the pair (876, I) was removed from index 77 by setting the slot directly to None.
description: The entries at bucket 78 and in the next two slots are still present. They are grayed out because the empty bucket earlier in the sequence cuts off the search. The indices of 676 and 776 are unlabeled, but their positions immediately after 78 imply indices 79 and 80.

frames.explanation: A lookup for 276 first compares it with key 076 in bucket 76. They differ. It then finds None in bucket 77 and stops early, never reaching (276, E) in bucket 78. Lookups for 676 and 776 also start at bucket 76 and stop at 77.
frames.title: Deletion with open addressing

result: When lookup stops at a genuinely empty slot, None, deletion cannot simply empty the slot. The text introduces a lazy deletion marker, TOMBSTONE, so lookup continues past a deleted bucket. The figure shows the broken probe sequence before this marker is introduced.
summary: Setting a deleted bucket directly to None in an open-addressed hash table breaks the linear probe sequence. A lookup may then incorrectly report that a colliding element farther along the sequence is absent.
